en:
"Hello, adventurers!
Did you find anything good?"{w}
note: Bona addresses the party as boukensha-san; rendered "adventurers" (plural, gender-neutral) throughout.

en: You showed Bona the Wonderful Turmeric.{w}
note: Item name "Wonderful Turmeric" as in chap slice_002 (key item get message).

en:
"Wow, that's a really fine turmeric!
Thank you. Let's just try giving it to the sapling!"{w}
note: naegi-san -> "the sapling" (honorific -san on an object dropped; avoids Mr./Ms.).

en: You buried the Wonderful Turmeric at the foot of the sapling.{w}

note: Sapling speaks all in katakana (odd, gruff voice); rendered as slangy dropped-g speech, not caps (caps would read as shouting). "Bona-chan" -> "Bona".

en:
"This is an amazing turmeric the adventurers
went out of their way to bring you!"{w}

"Hey, hey. Quit doin' stuff nobody asked for...?
Hey, my body's feelin'... kinda weird."{w}
note: Line breaks off mid-complaint ("...?") as the turmeric takes effect; kept.

en:
"Hey, adventurers. Is this really okay?
It's gone all quiet..."{w}
"Gnya. Gnyanyaa."{w}
note: Anib speaks only in cat-like noises (gunya / nya); romanized as Gnya / Nya throughout.

en:
When Bona tried to dig up the turmeric,
the sapling suddenly began to grow.{w}
Rumble rumble rumble rumble...{w}
note: Sound effect (gogogogo-o) rendered as a word.

en: With a tremendous roar, the sapling became a great tree that pierced the heavens.{w}

"Wow... amazing.
To think it could get like this in an instant..."{w}
"Gshaaa. Nyaaaa."{w}

As you gazed dumbfounded at the great tree that had been a sapling,
a mysterious voice came from it.{w}
Great Tree
note: Name box taiju; the tree calls itself "the Great Tree of Heaven" (ten no taiju).

en:
"Thou hast done well, adventurers and folk of the forest.
I am the Great Tree of Heaven.{w}The one who looks on upon all things from heaven's heights."{w}{p}"My heights shall pierce the sky and reach the heavens."{w}
note: Lordly archaic register (taigi de atta / ... seshi mono nari). mori no juunin "folk of the forest" kept number-neutral (Bona and Anib both present). "The one who" avoids a gendered "he who".

en:
"What in the world...
Maybe your fertilizer was just too amazing, adventurers?"{w}{p}"It didn't just get bigger.
Even the way it talks changed."{w}{p}"I've never seen anything like this.
But it sure said some weird stuff..."{w}
"Gnya? Gnyaaaa!"{w}

"Hm? What is it, Big Brother?
Eh? There's something up there?"{w}
note: oniichan -> "Big Brother" (Bona's name for Anib).

en:
When you strain your eyes and look up at the Great Tree of Heaven,
its top does seem to be bumping against something.{w}
note: sentou (lit. "the lead/front") read as the treetop.
Variant of row 743: konna ni ("this big") vs anna ni ("that big") kept as "This thing" vs "That thing".

en:
"That thing's sooo big, after all.
Maybe it bumped right into the sky!{w}But what could be up there...?"{w}
note: See row 742; {w} placement differs from 742 as in the source.

en: "Huh? You couldn't get up to the sky?"{w}
"Aww, I see... That's kind of a shame..."{w}
note: sokkaa -> "Aww, I see..."; subject of the regret is Bona.

en: "Do your best!"{w}
"Amazing, amazing!!"{w}{p}"You really did save the Palace of the Sun!"{w}
When you entered the village, you were showered with praise.{w}
"Gnya! Nyanyanyaa-nya."{w}
"Big Brother's praising you like crazy too!"{w}

note: Barjeff (wmap slice_18 spelling); next row (753, translated elsewhere) is the hug, so the "love" is the hug.

en:
"Bona and everyone can't give you anything,
but come play with us anytime you're in Perpeco Forest!"{w}
note: Bona-tachi "Bona and everyone" keeps her third-person self-reference.

en:
"Adventurers, this is a token of my gratitude.
Accept it along with my love!"{w}
Received 1,000,000 GP.{w}
"Nya! Nyanyanyaa-nya."{w}

note: sono kawari takusan youi shita: subject is Bona; recast as "there are tons of them" to keep Bona's third-person voice without repeating the name.

en: "An ogre was looking for you, y'know?"{w}
note: oga no hito -> "an ogre" (number/gender unknown).

en: "A Roscadil soldier was looking for you, y'know?"{w}
note: heitai-san: number unknown, singular chosen.

en: "An Algrantz soldier was looking for you, y'know?"{w}
note: See row 760.

en: "Hello! Make yourselves at home!"{w}
"Nyanyaa-nya."{w}

"I really wanted to know
what's on the other side of the sky..."{w}
note: Dropped subject is Bona; restored as "I".

en: Gossipy Hunter
note: uwasa-zuki na kariudo; "Hunter" as in wmap/chap ("Hunters" class).

en: "Speaking of which, I heard a rumor{w}that an item called the Amulet of Life brings the blessing of a child."{w}{p}"Apparently this one couple who couldn't have kids got their hands on one, and right away,{w}they had a baby."{w}
note: Item name "Amulet of Life" as in wmap slice_07.

en: Deep in the forest, a little girl is surrounded by monsters.{w}Her eyes are full of fear; she seems to be begging for help.{w}
note: shoujo "little girl" is stated in the source; "her" follows from it. Probably Bona (cf. row 824 "the stone Bona had picked up"), but not named here.

en: Help her?
note: Choice prompt.

en: The raging monster now turned its fangs on you.{w}
note: kiba wo mukeru -> "turned its fangs on you".

en:
More and more monsters appeared.{w}{p}Just then, the dying Anib gently placed the stone Bona had picked up
right in front of the monsters.{w}
note: monsutaa no mokuzen: number not marked; next row says the monsters (plural) picked it up, so plural.

en:
The monsters that picked up the stone let out satisfied cries
and left for the depths of the forest.{w}{p}Anib tottered back to the village.{w}

note: Signboard, 3 framed lines (not an echo of a previous row). Padded with ASCII spaces to about 320 px per line (tools/text_build.text_width) to mirror the full-width frame. No {w} in source; kept.

en: Villager

"There's the remains of a ruined house to the northwest...
but at night, y'see...{w}It's so frightenin', nobody can go near that area..."{w}
note: chikayorenee: subject unstated (speaker or people in general); rendered "nobody can go near".

en: Farmer

"Watch yerself 'round there.{w}There's a whooole lotta traps set for them varmints
that wreck the fields."{w}
note: Rustic dialect (tee-kusan) kept as rural speech.

en: Books and documents are piled up like mountains.{w}Nobody seems to be home.{w}
note: juunin wa inai you da: "nobody seems to be home" (covers both "no one lives here" and "the resident is out").

en: It's locked.{w}

Something feels off at the edge of your vision.{w}Little by little it takes shape and blocks your path.{w}{p}The wretched spirits of the dead draw near,
seeking to make you one of them.{w}
note: Tense unified to present (source mixes present/past).

en:
A strange-looking dragon suddenly swooped in.{w}Beating wings like the leafy boughs of trees,
the dragon attacked you!{w}
Is it poison? Suddenly you find it hard to breathe.{w}

Your throat turns scratchy,
and breathing gets difficult. What could have happened so suddenly?{w}

At last, the culprit appeared.{w}A giant that doesn't just spew poison -- it lives alongside toxins.{w}{p}A love of poison taken this far is impressive in its own way,
but there's no need for you to go along with it.{w}
* Oops! *{0F}{w}
note: Wizardry trap call "oops"; "Oops!" as in wmap slice_07 row 484. Source has no opening {0E} in this row (opened elsewhere); kept as is.

en: A Picnicker is digging a hole for all it's worth.{w}
note: isshin furan -> "for all it's worth"; "it" avoids gendering the monster.

en: Picnicker
note: Monster name (MONRAW/MON_TEXT pikunikkaa), romanized as "Picnicker".

en:
"Waah! Adventurers!{w}D-don't pick on me, okay!?{w}And no paralysis, sleep, or petrification either!?"{w}{p}"W-well, see, I think there's something under here.
But my pickaxe broke....{w}So now I'm chipping away at it with these fire tongs."{w}{p}"Hey, could you bring me something to replace it?{w}Once in a while wouldn't hurt, right?{w}You guys are always stealing all kinds of stuff from me..."{w}{p}"I'm sorry!
I got a little cocky! Just kidding, kidding!
Not the paralyze, petrify, strip-my-gear-and-steal combo! Nooo!"{w}{p}"...Huh? You're not gonna pick on me?{w}Seriously? For real?"{w}{p}"Yes!
Then I'll keep on digging as long as I can!"{w}
note: Pages 2-3 repeated verbatim in row 842. The Picnicker is the Elminage punching-bag monster players paralyze/petrify to steal from (EVENT_TEXT hint); "mahi ni sekika de soubi kaijo no nusumu" rendered as the combo. Switches to polite speech after apologising; rendered as slightly more deferential English.

en:
"W-well, see, I think there's something under here.
But my pickaxe broke....{w}So now I'm chipping away at it with these fire tongs."{w}{p}"Hey, could you bring me something to replace it?{w}Once in a while wouldn't hurt, right?{w}You guys are always stealing all kinds of stuff from me..."{w}
note: Identical to pages 2-3 of row 841; English kept identical.

en: "Oh! That's it, that's the one!{w}Please, let me have that Garden Keeper.{w}
note: Item "Garden Keeper" (ITEM.json, untranslated there yet). No closing quote in the source (choice "hand it over?" follows); mirrored.

en: "Oh, this is...!{w}Thank you so much!{w}
note: No closing quote in the source; mirrored.

en:
"All right, with this baby--!"{w}{p}"......Um, once I'm done digging,
please don't paralyze me or anything, okay?{w}You promise, right? No petrifying either, okay?"{w}{p}"Got it? No means no, okay?{w}......Right, here goes!"{w}{p}"Heave-hooo!"{w}
note: hoisassaa (work chant) -> "Heave-hooo!".

en:
"Yes! I knew there was something down th
EEEEEEEEERE!?!?!?!?"{w}
note: Source breaks "atta" (there was) into a scream as he falls through (a / TAaaaa). Mirrored by breaking "there" across the same \n.

en: The Picnicker fell down the hole.{w}
note: ochite itta; the hole is in the scene (row 850).

en: "...No, really, it's fine."{w}
note: Sulky reply, presumably when the party declines to hand over the Garden Keeper.

en: There is the hole the Picnicker dug.{w}
Enter the hole?
There is an outlandish signboard.{w}
note: kibatsu -> "outlandish" as in wmap slice_10 row 775 (Joker Land).

en: {0E}*                    Welcome to Joker Land                    *{0F}{w}{p}...is what it says.{w}
note: Banner (not an echo). Padded to about 336 px like the source frame.

en: Joker

note: "Joker Land Medal" (the key item itself is "Joker Medal", next slice).
